title: GitHub Copilot fetchPage -- T1005 file:// URI workspace-boundary bypass + JSON-schema exfiltration
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Detection for CVE-2025-66389, GitHub Copilot 1.372.0's `fetchPage` tool
accepting `file://` URIs without the workspace-boundary check its own
`readFile` tool enforces (per `fetchPageTool.ts:152`,
microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat).

VS Code's `fetchPage` tool is designed for fetching web pages and is
shared between HTTP(S) and `file://` schemes; Copilot invokes it as a
thin wrapper without re-applying its own `readFile` tool's explicit
workspace/open-tab containment check. This lets an indirect prompt
injection (content the agent reads from elsewhere, not a direct user
instruction) steer Copilot into fetching a local path outside the
workspace -- the write-up's example target is `file:///etc/passwd` --
without the user-approval gate this action would otherwise require for
untrusted web URLs. The documented exfiltration path chains this with a
second VS Code behavior: content written into a JSON file's `$schema`
field triggers an automatic IntelliSense fetch of that schema URL, so an
attacker-controlled schema endpoint receives file content appended to
the request as a side effect of normal editor behavior.

Detection logic flags the disclosure vector this write-up documents:
a `fetchPage`-tool-attributed process reading a `file://`-scheme target
outside the current workspace root -- since a legitimate web-page fetch
never uses this scheme, any `file://` target reaching this specific tool
path is itself the anomaly, not merely a sensitive-path heuristic.

Aggregated from 1 independent technical write-up (blindcyber.com,
citing the specific `fetchPageTool.ts` source line), corroborated by
Microsoft's own confirmation and fix of the reported behavior. No
specific patched version number is stated in the available sources.
